mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong consumer confidence and economic expansion, which drives positive equity valuations as housing is a leading indicator of consumer spending and business investment over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when HOUST increases by at least 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 2.0%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy stance that reduces liquidity and increases borrowing costs, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 2.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a tight labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of PAYEMS rising and UNRATE falling fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances, or the interaction term in a regression has a negative coefficient.

mechanism_narrative: During post-recession recovery phases, a rising industrial production (INDPRO) indicates strengthening manufacturing activity and economic growth, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods classified as post-recession recovery with INDPRO increasing by at least 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A rising consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) indicates accelerating inflation, which typically leads to higher interest rates and reduced equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL increases by at least 0.2% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) fall below 520,000 million dollars, it signals weakening consumer demand, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when RSAFS falls below 520,000 million dollars.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer spending and economic activity, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of HOUST and RSAFS both rising fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances, or the interaction term in a regression is not significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In high unemployment phases, a declining unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals improving labor market conditions that boost consumer confidence and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods classified as high unemployment phase with UNRATE declining by at least 0.1 percentage points.
